basai-wetland-urbanising.jpg.commons_description: View of Basai Wetland with aquatic vegetation and urbanising areas in the backdrop, Gurgaon (Gurugram), Haryana, India
basai-wetland-urbanising.jpg.used_for: Hero. Basai wetland under a complete mat of water hyacinth, a line of large-diameter water pipes stacked along the far bank, and a wall of residential towers in the haze behind. The whole story in one frame: the wetland closing over, the pipe network that replaces it, and the demand that paid for the pipes.

baoli-ghaus-ali-shah-farrukhnagar.jpg.commons_description: Baoli Ghaus Ali Shah, a stepwell in historic town of Farrukhnagar. Haryana
baoli-ghaus-ali-shah-farrukhnagar.jpg.used_for: Chapter 1, 'A town on a seasonal river'. The 18th-century stepwell at Farrukhnagar - a tehsil that still appears in GMDA's water-body register - with arcaded galleries, descending steps and the well shaft at the bottom. Completely dry.

behrampur-village-construction.jpg.commons_description: Gurgaon is a city of dichotomies. On one side you have multi story buildings that stand as the symbol of infrastructural development and on the other side you have villages and construction side.
behrampur-village-construction.jpg.used_for: Chapter 2, 'Twelve years, eight times the ground'. An unpaved lane in Behrampur with half-built brick terraces, exposed rebar and rubble - the municipal limit arriving at a village. Geotagged inside Gurugram.

najafgarh-jheel-survey-1840.jpg.commons_title: File:Map of the general plan of villages surveyed in Najafgarh Jheel, by William Brown, 1840–41 (F03-14).jpg
najafgarh-jheel-survey-1840.jpg.commons_description: Map of the general plan of villages surveyed in Najafgarh Jheel, by William Brown, 1840–41. F.3/14. – NAJAFGARH - General plan of villages surveyed in the Nujufghur Jheel. Scale 1" - 4 miles. By William Brown. 1840–41. MS.
najafgarh-jheel-survey-1840.jpg.used_for: Chapter 6, 'Gurugram is Delhi's problem too'. William Brown's 1840-41 manuscript survey of the Najafgarh Jheel, the lake Gurugram's runoff still drains into before it reaches Delhi as the Najafgarh drain.

_rejected.File:Najafgarh Drain - Aerial View - New: Fetched and examined, then rejected. The identification rests entirely on the uploader's title: the Commons description is only 'This photograph has been taken in India', there is no geotag, and the channel in the frame has broad natural meanders with floodplain farmland, which reads more like the Yamuna than the largely channelised Najafgarh drain. Captioning it as Gurugram's outflow would be a claim we cannot check. Replaced by the 1840 survey map, whose title is its content.
_rejected.File:JOHAD OF VILLAGE MEHRA.jpg: Rejected on location. A fine johad photograph, but geotagged 28.564,76.155 - Charkhi Dadri district, roughly 90 km west and outside Gurugram's bbox (76.64-77.25 E). Using it to illustrate Gurugram's johads would imply a place it is not.

_note: Provenance for every image in /public/images/story/gurugram. All from Wikimedia Commons; CC BY / CC BY-SA / public domain only. Every candidate was DOWNLOADED AND LOOKED AT before selection, not chosen from its title - one had a Commons caption describing towers that are not in the frame, and the alt text here describes the pixels rather than the caption. Candidates rejected on location or on an unverifiable identification are listed under _rejected with the reason, so they are not re-fetched. Chapters 3 (groundwater) and 5 (the tanker market) run without images: Commons has no borewell, tubewell or water-tanker photograph for Haryana that we could find, and an illustrative stand-in from another state would be worse than nothing.
